_about: Dev-only critical advisories, disclosed rather than waived. scripts/audit-deps.mjs compares this list against `npm audit --json` in both directions: a dev-tree critical that is not named here fails, and an entry named here that the tree no longer has also fails, because a register that keeps a closed vulnerability is a false statement about the product. Packages with a critical in the SHIPPED tree (`npm audit --omit=dev`) are not registrable at all — that half has no exception path.
_verifiedBy: npm ls vitest --omit=dev  ->  `-- (empty)`  (the runner is not in the installed production tree)
no file under src/ imports vitest, and next.config sets output: 'standalone', so the deployed trace never contains it
npm ls dompurify -> one copy at 3.4.17 with the override, two copies (monaco on 3.4.8) without it (measured 2026-10-23)

closed.how_it_got_into_production: It did not get there by accident: `shadcn`, a scaffolding CLI, sat in `dependencies`, so `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` -> `express` -> `proxy-addr` was 276 packages of server stack in the shipped tree. Moved to `devDependencies` in the same change that added this gate.
closed.scope_note: The advisory is about a trust-subnet check in `proxy-addr`, which the app's own per-IP limits do not use: `npm ls proxy-addr` resolves it only under the shadcn CLI path, and this repo's request path is Next.js middleware (`src/proxy.ts`), not express. Bumping it to 2.0.8 is still the right move — it removes the critical from the developer tree too.
closed.note: Listed here so the reason the shipped tree is empty is readable, not because anything is open. scripts/audit-deps.mjs does not read this array.

closed.title: Vitest: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read via @vitest/mocker redirect mock
closed.note: Closed by the vitest 5 major on 2026-10-09. The runner's own test suite passed unchanged except three constructor mocks (`vi.fn(() => x)` -> `vi.fn(function () { return x; })`): vitest 5 no longer lets an arrow-built mock be `new`-ed, and the products under test construct AudioContext.

closed.title: Tinypool: prototype-pollution gadget in worker options / run() options leads to RCE
closed.note: Closed by removing the dependency: vitest 5.0.3 no longer depends on tinypool at all (`grep '"node_modules/tinypool"' package-lock.json` -> 0 hits), so there is no vulnerable version in the tree. The fix for this row was never an override — vitest 3.2.7 pins ^1.1.1, and putting an unsupported worker pool under the runner is how a green stops meaning anything.

closed.title: Unauthenticated RCE in Image Optimization with SVG, SSRF in the same API, SSG/ISR cache poisoning in self-hosted builds, Server Action DoS, metadata-route information disclosure
closed.how_it_got_into_production: It is the framework: `dependencies.next` is pinned exactly, and `output: 'standalone'` means the self-hosted path is the one the cache-poisoning advisories describe. 16.4.2 is the first release outside the vulnerable ranges — the two newest advisories cover '<=16.4.0', so 16.3.8 would have left the Image Optimization RCE open.
closed.scope_note: Exposure here is concrete, not theoretical: `next.config.ts` allows three remote image hosts (Google, GitHub avatars, dicebear) for OAuth avatars, so /_next/image is reachable with attacker-influenced inputs. The resume path rejects SVG; the image optimiser is a separate surface.
closed.note: Closed 2026-10-23 by the version move. `npm ls next` reports 16.4.2 and `npm run audit:deps` reports shipped criticals=0.

closed.title: Eight sanitizer-bypass advisories: ALLOWED_ATTR pollution via setConfig, trusted-types policy surviving clearConfig, IN_PLACE hook removal leaving a detached subtree executable, CUSTOM_ELEMENT_HANDLING bypass, SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES split-expression bypass, SMIL guard skip
closed.how_it_got_into_production: Transitively, three ways: `monaco-editor` (the interview scratchpad) pins 3.4.8 exactly, `jspdf` (the dossier export) and `mermaid` each accept a range. Without an `overrides` entry npm resolves two copies — `npm ls dompurify` shows monaco still on 3.4.8 while the others take 3.4.17 — so the parent that matters is the one that will not move on its own, and `package.json` now forces 3.4.17.
closed.scope_note: The app never calls DOMPurify itself (zero references under src/); it is reached through monaco's and jspdf's own sanitisation of rendered content. The app's own HTML sink is `message-card.tsx` via `escapeHtml`, which is a different mechanism and is pinned by `security-surface.test.ts`.
closed.note: Closed 2026-10-23 by the override. Revisit by dropping the override once monaco-editor ships a range that includes 3.4.17; `npm ls dompurify` is the check.
